draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Basavanagudi! The name literally means bull temple, after Dodda Basavana Gudi, said to be one of the biggest Nandi temples in the world. It's one of Bengaluru's oldest neighbourhoods, with shops on DVG Road going back to the 1920s.
draft.hungryLine: This is old-school Bengaluru food country, so go for dosas on DVG Road in Gandhi Bazaar.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Bugle Rock is an 11 min walk, and the Bull Temple sits right beside it, about 13 minutes away. Gandhi Bazaar is an 11 min walk too.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Climb up into Bugle Rock park and sit on the old rock looking out over the neighbourhood.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Bugle Rock is a hump of peninsular gneiss about 3,000 million years old, and scientists take a real interest in it.

spots.name: Dodda Basavana Gudi
spots.detail: 13 min walk · A giant stone Nandi that keeps getting fresh layers of butter

spots.name: Bugle Rock
spots.detail: 11 min walk · Ancient rock with a Kempe Gowda watchtower on top

spots.name: Gandhi Bazaar
spots.detail: 11 min walk · Flower and condiment stalls along DVG Road

legends.title: The sunset bugle
legends.body: At sunset a sentry on the watchtower is said to have blown a bugle and held up a torch that the city's other three towers could see. It told people all was safe, and a different call warned of intruders.

legends.title: A river from the bull's feet
legends.body: Two old inscriptions near the temple say the Vrishabhavati river starts at the feet of the Basava idol. From there it flows west.

tips.title: Catch the groundnut fair.
tips.body: Kadalekaayi Parishe fills the temple area on the last Monday and Tuesday of Karthika Maasa, with farmers offering their first groundnuts.

tips.title: Shop Gandhi Bazaar early.
tips.body: The market runs from about 6 a.m. and gets extra crowded before festivals when people buy puja items.

story.title: Ancient rock
story.body: Bugle Rock, a sudden rise of gneiss, is reckoned to be about 3,000 million years old. Its hollows were once used to light lamps.

story.title: Watchtowers
story.body: Kempe Gowda II, who came to power in 1585, is credited with four watchtowers marking Bangalore's limits. One stood on Bugle Rock, the southern edge, with a view across the city.

story.title: DVG Road
story.body: Shops on DVG Road, some of the oldest in the city, date back to the 1920s and 1930s. Vidyarthi Bhavan, a vegetarian restaurant, opened in Gandhi Bazaar in 1943.

story.title: First private engineering college
story.body: B.M.S. College of Engineering opened on Bull Temple Road, diagonally opposite the Bull Temple. It's known as the first private engineering college in India.

story.title: Metro arrives
story.body: Several Green Line metro stations serving Basavanagudi, including National College and Lalbagh, opened on 18 June 2017.
